No templates found. Maybe the product SMILES is wrong. Perhaps the target molecule is the ester (the one we have) and we need to find template that reduces it to aldehyde (i.e., forward reaction is reduction, but template is retrosynthetic: break C-O bond to give ester precursor? Actually retrosynthetic step: from product (aldehyde) we go to precursor (ester). The template applied to product yields ester precursors (the list we have). So the template is the reverse of reduction: it forms ester from aldehyde (i.e., adds O-alkyl). So the template's forward reaction is ester formation (maybe "aliphatic hydroxyls" + "carboxylic acid" -> "carboxylic ester"). But the description says forward reaction is DIBAL-H reduction, but we are doing retrosynthesis, so template is reduction. However the template database likely contains forward reaction as the transformation (i.e., reduction). So functional groups broken in forward: "carboxylic ester" (or acid) broken, functional groups formed: "aldehydes". But we didn't find. Maybe the molecule we should search is the ester (precursor) not the aldehyde. Let's try using one of the precursor SMILES as molecule_smiles, and search for templates that break ester to give aldehyde (i.e., forward reaction is reduction). So functional_groups_broken: ["carboxylic esters"]? The precursor has a carboxylic acid not ester. Actually the precursor SMILES includes "C(=O)O" which is acid. So broken group is "aliphatic carboxylic acid". Let's try search with that molecule.

Use first precursor SMILES: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO". Search with broken: ["aliphatic carboxylic acid"], formed: ["aldehydes"].
